title: 2.2 Inductive and Deductive Reasoning

icans: I can use inductive reasoning to describe a pattern and make a conjecture.
I can show a conjecture is false with a counterexample.
I can use the Laws of Detachment and Syllogism to reach a conclusion.

vocab: an unproven statement that is based on _______________
finding a pattern in specific cases and then writing a _____________ for the general case
a specific case for which a _____________ is false
using facts, ______________, accepted properties, and the laws of logic to form a logical argument

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Inductive reasoning: look at examples, find a _______________, and make a conjecture.

blocks.stem: Describe the pattern and find the next number: 3, 7, 11, 15, …

notes: Counterexample: to show a conjecture is false, you need only _______________ counterexample.

blocks.stem: Find a counterexample: “The difference of two positive numbers is always positive.”

notes: Law of Detachment: if p → q is true and p is true, then _______________ is true.
Law of Syllogism: if p → q and q → r are true, then _______________ is true.

blocks.stem: What can you conclude? “If two segments have the same length, then they are congruent. AB = CD = 5.”
Write the statement that follows: “If a figure is a square, then it is a rectangle.” “If a figure is a rectangle, then it has four right angles.”

tickets.stem: Find a counterexample: “If a number is divisible by 2, then it is divisible by 4.”
